lesson_title: Why Your Calculator Says Math Error
hook_text: 12 ÷ 0. Your calculator refuses. It is not broken — it knows something you might not.
clip_script: Now the anchor. Twelve divided by zero. Apply the definition without flinching: what number, multiplied by zero, gives twelve? Try four: four times zero is zero, not twelve. Try one hundred: one hundred times zero is zero. Try a million. Every whole number, every fraction, every number you will ever meet, multiplied by zero, gives zero. Nothing times zero gives twelve. The multiplication question has NO answer — and therefore the division has no answer. Twelve divided by zero is undefined. Undefined is a precise technical word. It does not mean the answer is zero. It does not mean the answer is infinity. It means that no number satisfies the definition.
visual_style: A calculator screen fills the frame; candidate numbers 4, 100, 1 000 000 fly at a times-zero gate and each collapses to 0 with a thud; the screen finally flashes MATH ERROR and the word UNDEFINED is stamped in red.
pacing: Three quick failed attempts, a beat of silence, then the stamp.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for the sharing picture and the runaway pattern.
